note: 'Consider/considered' (regard) became 'look at', losing the sense picked up by 'consideration' in the next paragraph.
replacement: Ideas and feelings followed one another, and heart and head came into play. Men went on laying aside their original wildness, and their private connections grew more intimate every day as their limits widened. They got used to gathering before their huts round a large tree. Singing and dancing, the true offspring of love and leisure, became the amusement, or rather the occupation, of the men and women who gathered there with nothing else to do. Each began to consider the rest and to wish to be considered in turn. Thus public esteem came to carry a value. The best singer or dancer, the handsomest, the strongest, the most dexterous or the most eloquent, came to be the most considered. This was the first step toward inequality, and at the same time toward vice. These first distinctions gave rise to vanity and contempt on the one side, and to shame and envy on the other. The fermentation caused by these new leavens ended by producing combinations fatal to innocence and happiness.

note: Added 'may have' weakens the source's flat 'suggested'.
replacement: How men first came to know and use iron is hard to conjecture. We cannot suppose they would of themselves think of digging ore out of a mine and preparing it for smelting before they knew what would come of it. Nor have we much reason to suppose some accidental fire made the discovery, since mines form only in barren places, bare of trees and plants. It looks as if nature had taken pains to keep the fatal secret from us. Only the extraordinary accident of a volcano remains. By throwing out metallic substances already in fusion, it suggested to the onlookers the idea of imitating what nature did. We must also conceive them as having uncommon courage and foresight, to undertake so laborious a work with so distant a prospect of advantage. Yet such qualities are found together only in minds more advanced than we can suppose those of the first discoverers to have been.

note: 'Only' is added; the source says equality might have been sustained, not only under that condition.
replacement: In this state of affairs, equality could have been kept up if individuals had had equal talents, and if, for example, the use of iron and the consumption of commodities had always balanced exactly. But nothing kept this balance, and it was soon upset. The strongest did the most work; the most skilful made the best use of his labor; the most ingenious found ways to lessen his labor. The husbandman needed more iron, or the smith more corn. Both labored equally, yet one gained a great deal by his work while the other could hardly support himself. So natural inequality unfolds itself gradually together with that of combination. As circumstances differ, the differences between men develop; they grow more noticeable and more lasting in their effects, and they begin to influence the lot of individuals in the same proportion.
